item.title: Vicksburg police investigate early morning crash, separate shooting near Circle K - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
VICKSBURG – Vicksburg police are investigating a three-vehicle crash and a separate shooting that happened early Sunday near Circle K.

The Vicksburg Police Department said officers were first dispatched at 2:46 a.m. to the area of Clay Street and Old Highway 27 for a three-vehicle crash.

Police said one of the vehicles caught fire and injuries were reported, though the extent of those injuries was not immediately known.

While officers were responding to that scene, shots were fired around 3 a.m. in the area of Circle K, according to police.

Officers later found multiple shell casings at the scene. No injuries had been reported in connection with the shooting, police said.

Preliminary information indicates the crash and the shooting do not appear to be related, though both remain under active investigation.

Anyone with information about the shooting is asked to contact the Vicksburg Police Department or Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS.

item.title: Two people shot during trail ride event in Tunica County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUNICA COUNTY – Two people were wounded Saturday evening in a shooting at a trail ride event in Tunica County, according to the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office.

The sheriff’s office said multiple 911 calls came in around 6:09 p.m. reporting shots fired at a trail ride being held in Dundee on Dubbs Road by Muddy River Delta Farm.

Deputies and first responders were dispatched to the scene, where they found two people suffering from apparent gunshot wounds.

Authorities said both victims were treated at the scene by Pafford and then transported by Wings by Pafford AirOne to hospitals for further treatment.

The investigation remains active and ongoing.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office at 662-363-1411. Anonymous tips can be submitted to Crime Stoppers at 662-910-0400. Officials said information leading to an arrest could result in a reward of up to $1,000.

item.title: Rape suspect fatally shot by U.S. Marshals during warrant service in Indianola - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
INDIANOLA — The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation is looking into a fatal officer-involved shooting involving the U.S. Marshals Service that happened March 30 at a home on Mill Street.

According to MBI, agents with the U.S. Marshals Service were attempting to serve a rape warrant on a person at a home in Indianola when the subject displayed a weapon toward the agents.

An agent then fired a weapon, striking the subject and causing fatal injuries, MBI said.

Authorities said no agents suffered serious physical injuries.

MBI said it is continuing to gather evidence and assess the incident. Once the investigation is complete, the agency will share its findings with the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office.

Officials said the information released so far is preliminary and could change.

item.title: MISSING IN MISSISSIPPI: Frank Garcia, Chickasaw County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
CHICKASAW COUNTY — A Houston man who walked away from his home carrying his belongings in February 1994 has never been found, and investigators are still seeking information that could help solve his disappearance.

Frank Garcia, a 35-year-old Hispanic man, was last seen on Feb. 16, 1994, walking away from his residence on Highway 8 East in Houston. He was carrying two garbage bags of clothes, a 19-inch television and a box of important papers at the time.

Garcia was not reported missing until nearly a week later, when he failed to pick up two paychecks from his employer and no one had heard from him.

He is described as 5 feet, 5 inches tall, weighing approximately 140 pounds, with brown hair and brown eyes. Garcia has tattoos reading “Nancy” on one arm and “Ginger” on the other.

The case is being investigated by the Mississippi Department of Public Safety and the Chickasaw County Sheriff’s Department. Garcia remains missing as of the publication of this report.

Anyone with information on Garcia’s whereabouts is asked to contact the Mississippi Department of Public Safety at (662) 563-6400 or the Chickasaw County Sheriff’s Department at (662) 456-3513.

item.title: Lary Aaron to headline Legacy League Hot Stove event April 3 in Jackson - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Lary Aaron, son of baseball legend Hank Aaron, will make a special guest appearance April 3 at a Hot Stove event in Jackson to support the inaugural season of the Legacy League, organizers announced.

The event, sponsored by Colombean Coffee, is set for 2 p.m. at the Mississippi Sports Hall of Fame. It is free and open to the public and will feature a one-hour interview session, question-and-answer segment and autograph opportunities with former professional players.

Aaron, who followed his father into baseball, played outfield at Florida A&M University before being selected by the Atlanta Braves in the 32nd round of the 1981 MLB Draft. He spent two seasons in the Braves’ minor league system before transitioning into a long career in scouting, including nearly two decades with the Milwaukee Brewers organization.

Organizers said Aaron has remained active in mentoring athletes and promoting the values associated with his father’s legacy, including integrity and dedication to the sport.

Other scheduled guests for the event include former Braves and Falcons standout Brian Jordan, World Series champion Marquis Grissom and former Braves pitcher Jair Jurrjens.

The appearance is part of a promotional push ahead of the launch of the Legacy League, a developmental baseball league designed to provide opportunities for collegiate players. The league’s ownership group includes former professional athletes such as Tracy McGrady, Andruw Jones, Jordan, Jurrjens, Grissom and Bernard Gilkey.

League play is scheduled to begin May 26, with a 28-game season to be held at Smith-Wills Stadium.

item.title: Hinds County murder suspect arrested after two-vehicle crash in Jones County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
HINDS COUNTY – A 19-year-old man wanted on a capital murder warrant out of Hinds County was arrested Sunday night after deputies responded to a two-vehicle crash in Jones County.

Jackson teen arrested on capital murder charges

The crash happened around 8:29 p.m. at Moselle Seminary Road and U.S. Highway 11, according to the Jones County Sheriff’s Department. Authorities said the wreck was blocking lanes of traffic when deputies arrived.

Deputies Kalob Broadway and Will Ladd responded to the scene and, during the crash investigation, determined that one of the vehicle’s occupants, Zachary Stevens, was listed in the FBI’s National Crime Information Center database as wanted by the Hinds County Sheriff’s Office on a capital murder warrant.

Stevens was arrested at the scene and taken to the Jones County Adult Detention Facility, where he is being held pending extradition to Hinds County.

item.title: Five killed, one injured in train-van crash in Stone County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
STONE COUNTY – Five people were killed and a sixth was seriously injured Friday afternoon when a train collided with a van in Stone County, according to WLOX.

Stone County Sheriff Todd Stewart told WLOX the crash happened around 1 p.m. at Pump Branch Road, just off Highway 49. First responders had to cut their way through the woods to reach the wreckage, the station reported.

Authorities said six people were inside the van at the time of the crash. Stone County Coroner Wayne Flurry confirmed that five of them died at the scene, and the sixth person was airlifted to a hospital in New Orleans.

WLOX later reported the five people killed were identified as 26-year-old Ryan C. Peterson, 23-year-old Demarcus Perkins, 45-year-old Kristina Carver, and Carver’s two daughters, 22-year-old Emley Chamblee and 20-year-old Sarabeth Chamblee.

The station also reported that the railroad crossing at Pump Branch Road does not have crossing arms or lights. Stone County District 1 Supervisor Jimmy Springs told WLOX that crossarms are planned for the crossing, but installation could take up to a year.

item.title: Eight families displaced after apartment fire on West Capitol Street in Jackson - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Eight families were displaced Sunday morning after a fire damaged multiple units at an apartment complex on West Capitol Street, according to the Jackson Fire Department.

Firefighters were called at 8:49 a.m. Sunday to 1315 W. Capitol St., the Magnolia Apartments, for a reported structure fire.

When crews arrived, they found smoke and flames coming from the building, officials said.

After the fire was extinguished, the origin and cause could not immediately be determined, and a fire investigator was called to the scene.

Investigators later classified the cause of the fire as undetermined, according to the fire department. Officials said the investigation remains ongoing as additional information becomes available.

The fire damaged eight apartment units and displaced eight families, authorities said. The American Red Cross is assisting those affected.

No injuries were reported.

item.title: DARKHORSE DOGS: Meet Rayford, a handsome Border Collie mix looking for a home - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
BROOKHAVEN – Rayford is a young, energetic dog with good looks and a playful personality, and Brookhaven Animal Rescue League hopes the right family will come along soon to take him home.

Shelter staff say Rayford has been enjoying time with volunteers, including a recent outing with volunteer Dolores, who had fun spending time with him.

item.title: Casino burglary suspect caught by Tunica County K-9 after lengthy chase - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUNICA COUNTY – A Tunica man was arrested Friday night after authorities said he was linked to a vehicle burglary at a Robinsonville casino, then led deputies on a chase that ended in a crash and foot pursuit.

The Tunica County Sheriff’s Office said deputies were called around 9:14 p.m. Friday to a casino in Robinsonville after receiving a report of a vehicle burglary in the parking lot.

Witnesses provided a description of the suspects’ vehicle, and that information was broadcast to patrol deputies, according to the sheriff’s office.

At about 9:52 p.m., a deputy spotted a vehicle matching the description near Old Highway 61 and Casino Strip Drive and attempted a traffic stop. Authorities said the driver refused to stop, leading deputies on a high-speed chase before losing control of the vehicle and fleeing on foot.

Deputies then pursued the suspect on foot and used a sheriff’s office K-9 to make the arrest, officials said.

Authorities identified the suspect as Deonte Taylor, 20, of Tunica. Taylor suffered a dog bite during the apprehension and was treated at an area hospital before being taken to the Tunica County Jail.

Taylor was charged with failure to stop, possession of a stolen firearm, possession of burglary tools, conspiracy, burglary of a vehicle and felony fleeing.

The sheriff’s office said Taylor had also been out on bond in connection with a 2023 triple homicide case in Tunica County, where he faced capital murder and other charges.

Officials said Taylor was given a $45,000 bond on the new charges.

The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information is asked to contact CrimeStoppers at 662-910-0400 or the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office at 662-363-1411.

item.title: Attala County manhunt ends with suspect dead - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
ATTALA COUNTY – A man wanted in connection with a shooting that left two people dead in Attala County is now dead, according to the sheriff’s department. Attala County Sheriff Curtis Pope posted on Facebook early Monday that the suspect was killed while trying to enter someone’s home.

The suspect was identified as Christopher Hughes. Before his death, Carthage police had described him as armed and dangerous in connection with the Sunday shootings. The identities of the two victims had not been released as of Monday morning.

In response to the situation, the Kosciusko School District canceled three bus routes Monday for student safety. Those routes were 65-03, known as Culpepper, 81-14, known as Jamison, and 78-12, known as Ford. School officials asked parents who could transport their children to do so and said anyone unable to bring students to school should contact the school office.

Breezy News also reported that two additional routes, those of Mrs. Collins and Mrs. Veasley, would not run Monday.

School officials said the safety of students and staff remained their top priority.

item.title: Opera Mississippi to Perform 'Songs for a New World' in Jackson - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Opera Mississippi will bring Tony Award-winning composer Jason Robert Brown’s “Songs for a New World” to Duling Hall in Jackson on April 24-25, offering audiences two nights of professional musical theatre centered on themes of change, resilience and hope.

Tickets are $35 per person. Each evening begins with an Opera Happy Hour at 6 p.m., with the concert starting at 7 p.m. Duling Hall is located at 622 Duling Ave.

The production features four professional vocalists: John Christopher Adams, Maryann Kyle, Peter Lake and Sarah Stembel. They will be performing a song cycle that blends pop, gospel and contemporary musical theatre. Rather than a traditional narrative, the show presents a series of self-contained scenes depicting people at pivotal moments of transformation.

Brown, who won a Tony Award for “The Bridges of Madison County,” wrote “Songs for a New World” as his debut stage work. The piece has since become a staple of regional and professional musical theatre nationally.

Founded in 1945, Opera Mississippi is the ninth oldest continuously operating opera company in the United States and the state’s only professional opera company. The organization’s mission includes educational outreach, emerging artist development and preserving the operatic art form.

Tickets are available at operamississippi.org .

item.title: Mississippi Man, 83, Charged After Striking Firefighter With Vehicle - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON COUNTY — An 83-year-old Jackson County man is facing a felony charge after allegedly striking a U.S. Forest Service firefighter with his vehicle while attempting to bypass a road closure during an active forest fire Saturday evening.

Tommy Broadnax was charged with simple assault on a firefighter following the approximately 5:45 p.m. incident on Stephen Earl Drive in the Latimer Community, according to Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter.

Firefighters and U.S. Forest Service personnel had closed the roadway while working to contain a forest fire in the area. When Broadnax was told the road was closed, authorities said he became agitated and refused to comply with orders from first responders. A Forest Service firefighter attempted to stop him and repeat the warning, but Broadnax struck her with his vehicle, knocking her to the ground, before continuing down the road.

Broadnax was taken into custody without further incident. Under Mississippi law, simple assault on a firefighter is a felony offense.

The Jackson County Sheriff’s Office is asking anyone with additional information to contact the agency at (228) 769-3063.

item.title: Yee-haw & you're welcome: We're celebrating Quirky Country Music Song Titles Day - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
STATEWIDE — Every year on March 27th, country music fans and lovers of linguistic absurdity unite to celebrate one of the most delightfully niche holidays on the calendar: Quirky Country Music Song Titles Day. It’s a day to tip your hat to the poets, the heartbroken, and the genuinely unhinged wordsmiths and writers who gave us some of the most wonderfully weird song titles in music history.

Your Hometown Country US 96.3’s Traci Lee immediately thought of the song “Ticks” by Brad Paisley, because the deeper meaning is… “I wanna check you for ticks.” US 96.3’s morning show host, Gordo, couldn’t immediately pick a favorite, but said he was sure it had something to do with tractors. Well guess what, Gordo, there’s a tractor in the top 5.

Country music has always had a special relationship with the ridiculous. While other genres sometimes aim for the profound or the cool, country music has never been afraid to get specific about being silly. Where else could a man earnestly record a song called “I’ve Been Flushed from the Bathroom of Your Heart” (and have it be Johnny Cash, no less) and have audiences sing along like, “Yeah, I’ve been there?”

The tradition runs deep. From Loretta Lynn and Conway Twitty harmonizing on “You’re the Reason Our Kids Are Ugly” to Bobby Bare asking the Lord to “Drop Kick Me Jesus Through the Goalposts of Life,” country music has long understood that life is funny, really messy, and worth writing songs about, no matter how absurd it sounds when you call the request line.

It seems like there’s actually a philosophy buried in the silliness. Country music titles tend to be hyper-specific: It’s a particular store, a particular animal, a particular piece of farm equipment. That specificity is what makes them so funny. “She Got the Gold Mine (I Got the Shaft)” by Jerry Reed isn’t just a joke. It’s a whole divorce settlement process summarized in a jaunty little country tune.

Here’s our Top 15:

“You’re the Reason Our Kids Are Ugly” — Conway Twitty & Loretta Lynn “She Got the Gold Mine (I Got the Shaft)” — Jerry Reed “I’ve Been Flushed from the Bathroom of Your Heart” — Johnny Cash “Dirty Old Egg-Sucking Dog” — Johnny Cash “She Thinks My Tractor’s Sexy” — Kenny Chesney “Get Your Tongue Outta My Mouth ‘Cause I’m Kissing You Goodbye” — Carlene Carter “I Still Miss You Baby, But My Aim’s Gettin’ Better” — various artists “If My Nose Was Running Money, I’d Blow It All on You” — Aaron Wilburn “Drop Kick Me Jesus Through the Goalposts of Life” — Bobby Bare “Tequila Makes Her Clothes Fall Off” — Joe Nichols “I’m Gonna Miss Her (The Fishin’ Song)” — Brad Paisley “It Wasn’t God Who Made Honky Tonk Angels” — Kitty Wells “One Piece at a Time” — Johnny Cash (about stealing a Cadillac part by part) “Redneck Yacht Club” — Craig Morgan “If You Can’t Bite, Don’t Growl” — various artists

So on March 27 of each year, while you’re two-stepping in your kitchen to the newest hits on Your Hometown Country US96.3, crying into your sweet tea over some 1994 ballad on 93.5 The Legend, or just sitting on the porch wondering why your dog looks at you like that, take a moment to appreciate the unsung heroes of country music: the title writers. The ones who looked at a blank page, thought about heartbreak, truck payments, and bad luck, and decided the only reasonable response was to take the humanity of it to the most ridiculous place possible.

Happy Quirky Country Music Song Titles Day, from Darkhorse Press. Now go call your mama. You know she worries.

item.title: STEPPING UP TO SERVE: Hal’s St. Paddy’s krewes bring joy to Children’s of Mississippi patients - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Patients at Children’s of Mississippi got a special dose of joy this week when krewes from Hal’s St. Paddy’s Parade & Festival brought a parade-sized celebration right to them, complete with mini floats and festive throws.

The visit tied one of Jackson’s most loved spring traditions directly to the children and families it helps support. Hal’s St. Paddy’s Parade, often described by organizers as a “green Mardi Gras,” is a longtime downtown Jackson celebration known for its colorful floats and community spirit. Organizers say the festival honors the legacy of Hal White, celebrates downtown Jackson and supports Children’s of Mississippi.

This year’s main parade is set for noon Saturday, March 28, in downtown Jackson. Festival events also include pet and children’s parades at Smith Park, part of a larger weekend celebration that has become a signature event for the capital city.

For the young patients who got an early visit, the parade came in a smaller form, but certainly made their days.

item.title: “Moonlight, Music and Meteors” Returns to Jackson with Symphony, Stargazing Event - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks is inviting the public to celebrate America’s 250th birthday with an evening of live music and stargazing at the fourth annual “Moonlight, Music, and Meteors” event on April 17.

The event, hosted at Mississippi Museum of Natural Science in LeFleur’s Bluff State Park, will run from 7:30 p.m. to 10 p.m. and feature a performance by the Mississippi Symphony Orchestra. Organizers say the concert will include music reflecting American history as well as astronomy-themed selections.

Tickets are $20 in advance online through noon April 16 and $25 at the door. Food vendors, including Skenny Burgers and The Pig and Pint, will be on site with concessions available for purchase.

In addition to the concert, attendees can interact with NASA Solar System Ambassadors and local astronomers, with opportunities to observe the night sky and potentially view the annual Lyrid meteor shower. Guests are encouraged to bring lawn chairs or blankets.

“This is a perfect reflection of what the museum strives to offer — memorable experiences that connect science, culture and community,” said museum director Angel Rohnke.

The event is a collaboration between the museum, the Mississippi Museum of Natural Science Foundation and the symphony orchestra, with support from the Mississippi Arts Commission and the National Endowment for the Arts.

Organizers say the event has become a popular annual gathering that brings together residents of all ages for music, education and outdoor recreation.

item.title: Mississippi reports first flu death of 2025-26 season - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – The Mississippi State Department of Health has confirmed the state’s first pediatric influenza death of the 2025-26 flu season.

The death was announced Friday. A pediatric flu death is defined as the death of a person younger than 18, according to the health department.

Officials did not release the child’s age, gender or location, citing privacy and respect for the family.

The death brings the total number of pediatric flu deaths in Mississippi to 28 since such deaths became reportable during the 2008-09 flu season, the department said.

State Epidemiologist Dr. Renia Dotson urged residents to get vaccinated.

“A vaccination won’t necessarily keep you from getting the flu, but it can reduce your risk of infection and is the best protection to keep you from a severe outcome,” Dotson said in a statement.

Health officials recommend that everyone 6 months and older receive an updated flu vaccine.

Flu season in Mississippi typically peaks between January and March, and the flu shot can take up to two weeks to provide immunity, according to the department.

Flu shots for eligible children 18 and younger are available at county health departments through the Vaccines for Children program. Insurance, Medicaid and the Children’s Health Insurance Program also are accepted for children’s flu shots, officials said.

Adults who are uninsured or underinsured can receive flu shots at county health department clinics. For insured adults, vaccines are widely available through private doctors, pharmacies and retail clinics.

item.title: Mississippi Correctional Institute for Women hosts resource fair for inmates nearing release - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PEARL – The Mississippi Correctional Institute for Women hosted a resource fair Thursday for inmates who are within three months of release, offering support and connections aimed at helping them transition back into society.

The Mississippi Department of Corrections said the event was held March 26 and was organized by Major Williestine Guise.

Officials said the fair featured booths from several organizations and agencies that provided information, encouragement and re-entry resources for the women preparing for release.

Participants included representatives from the Mississippi Department of Corrections Re-Entry Team, Hope Psychiatric Consultants of Pearl, VitalCore Health Strategies and Surge Staffing Company.

Attendees also had the opportunity to speak with the dean of Hinds Community College and the director of Crossroads Transitional Living Facility, according to MDOC. Representatives from Brown Bottling Group and Wayne-Sanderson Farms also took part.

Officials said booths offered pamphlets, brochures and other networking materials. Afterward, MDOC Deputy Commissioner Kelley Christopher delivered remarks intended to encourage and motivate the women.

The department said attendees also were provided a special meal and time to talk with one another about their future plans.

MDOC thanked Superintendent Katrina Reid for supporting the event and said it hopes to include even more vendors at future resource fairs.

item.title: Jackson Enacts New Parade Rules Ahead of Hal’s St. Paddy’s Day Celebration - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The City of Jackson will enforce new parade regulations during this year’s Hal’s St. Paddy’s Day Parade, restricting activities such as open-flame cooking, glass containers and certain vehicles in an effort to improve safety and crowd control downtown.

The ordinances, approved by the Jackson City Council in November 2025, apply to parade organizers, participants, vendors and spectators within the Downtown Business Improvement District during designated parade hours from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Under the new rules, grills, barbecues, smokers and other open-flame cooking devices are prohibited along the parade route unless specifically permitted by the city. Cooking with oils or grease is also banned without prior approval. In addition, glass containers — including bottles, jars and drinking glasses — are not allowed.

The ordinance also bars the use or presence of specialty vehicles such as all-terrain vehicles, golf carts and other low-speed or off-road vehicles unless authorized. Portable toilets may not be placed along the route without a city-issued permit.

City leaders also moved to prevent the early claiming of space along the parade route. Beginning four hours before the parade starts, individuals and groups are prohibited from fencing off or reserving public areas unless approved to protect landscaping.

Firearms are prohibited for paradegoers and participants, with exceptions for law enforcement officers and individuals allowed under state law for enhanced concealed carry.

The Jackson Police Department and Mississippi Capitol Police will enforce the rules, with officers stationed throughout the parade route and surrounding district. Violations could lead to confiscation of prohibited items, revoked permits, citations or removal from the area.

Mayor John Horhn said the changes are intended to make the annual event safer and more family-friendly while preserving its festive atmosphere.

“We are committed to making Hal’s St. Paddy’s Day Parade safe and enjoyable for everyone who comes downtown,” Horhn said. “These new parade rules will help keep families safe, reduce risks from things like open flames and glass, and make sure our first responders can do their jobs.”

Horhn encouraged attendees to plan ahead and comply with the updated regulations, including leaving prohibited items at home and following directions from law enforcement.

The mayor said the parade remains one of Jackson’s signature events and emphasized that the new rules are designed to support, not limit, the celebration.

Residents and visitors can review the full ordinance through the City Clerk’s Office or on the city’s website.

item.title: Greenville man charged with arson in house fire investigation - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GREENVILLE – A Greenville man has been charged with arson after police said he was identified in surveillance video connected to a house fire on Ridge Avenue.

The Greenville Police Department said officers were called around 7 a.m. March 21 to the 300 block of Ridge Avenue in reference to a house fire.

When officers arrived, they spoke with the homeowner, who said he had already extinguished the fire before police got there.

According to police, the homeowner told officers he reviewed surveillance video that showed a suspect spraying an unknown accelerant on the east side of the residence and setting the home on fire.

Witnesses identified the suspect in the video as Johnny Grandison, 34, of Greenville, police said.

Grandison was taken into custody and charged with arson. He is being held at the Washington County Regional Correctional Facility pending his initial appearance.

The Greenville Fire Department is continuing to investigate the case.

item.title: DeSoto County man sentenced to 30 years on child exploitation conviction - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
DESOTO COUNTY – A 42-year-old man was sentenced to 30 years in prison after being convicted of child exploitation, according to the DeSoto County District Attorney’s Office.

Christopher Stover was sentenced as a habitual offender under Mississippi law, officials said. Authorities said Stover was also a registered sex offender at the time of the offense.

Because of his habitual offender status, Stover must serve the full 30-year sentence day for day and is not eligible for early release, according to the district attorney’s office.

The case began with a cyber tip submitted through the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children, which alerted authorities to the illegal activity, officials said.

The DeSoto County Sheriff’s Office led the investigation. Authorities credited Investigator Jessica Palmer with building the case.

Assistant District Attorney Steven Jubera prosecuted the case, according to the district attorney’s office.

CARROLL COUNTY – A wildfire in Carroll County has burned approximately 1,800 acres near Coila, according to WTVA. The blaze began Wednesday night, Carroll County Fire Coordinator Jake Hurst told the station.

Firefighters have been working to contain the fire near County Road 145, Hurst said. He told WTVA that crews are monitoring about 30 nearby homes, but the structures were not considered to be in immediate danger.

The National Weather Service has warned of dangerous fire weather conditions in Mississippi, saying dry air, gusty winds and dry fuels could create explosive fire growth potential and allow wildfires to spread rapidly. The agency advised that open burning should not be attempted.

item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Attorney General’s Office has cleared law enforcement officers in five separate line of duty shootings across the state, while a sixth case has resulted in the indictment of a Laurel police officer.

In a statement released Friday, the office said it found the use of force justified in incidents occurring between March 2024 and February 2025 in multiple jurisdictions, following investigations conducted by the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation.

The reviewed cases include a March 31, 2024, shooting in Florence involving four deputies with the Rankin County Sheriff’s Office; an Aug. 2, 2024, incident in Clarksdale involving a police lieutenant and captain; an Aug. 8, 2024, shooting in Summit involving officers from both Summit and McComb police departments; a Sept. 8, 2024, incident in Jackson involving a city police officer; and a Feb. 16, 2025, shooting in Flowood involving two Flowood police officers.

Under Mississippi law, the Attorney General’s Office reviews officer-involved shootings after investigations by the state bureau. Officials said all five cases were determined to be legally justified uses of force under Section 45-1-6 of state code.

In a separate case, a Jones County Grand Jury indicted a Laurel Police Department officer on Feb. 23, 2026, on one count of aggravated assault stemming from an Oct. 23, 2023, officer-involved shooting in Laurel. According to the Brooks Law Firm, who is representing the child who was shot, the grand jury indicted Officer Jacob Giangrosso aggravated assault charges on February 23.

That case was also investigated by the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation and is being prosecuted by the Attorney General’s Office. Officials declined further comment, citing ongoing litigation.

No additional details about the indicted officer or the circumstances of the shooting were immediately released.

JACKSON – Jackson State University presents its first “History in Conversation,” a new discussion-based series exploring institutional milestones and honoring pioneers throughout JSU’s legacy.

item.title: Webster County Health Department to remain closed through April for renovations - Darkhorse Press

item.description:
WEBSTER COUNTY – The Webster County Health Department will remain closed through the month of April as remodeling work continues, according to the Mississippi State Department of Health.

item.title: Shilo Sanders highlights JSU's 2026 P.R.O.M. Promise event - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
By Anthony Howard Jackson State University

Jackson — Jackson State University hosted its 2026 P.R.O.M. Promise event, welcoming hundreds of high school students from the Jackson Public School District (JPS) for a day focused on empowerment, education and life preparation. This year’s event was highlighted by a special appearance from Shilo Sanders, whose message resonated strongly with attendees. Sanders, known for his leadership both on and off the field, shared personal insights on discipline, accountability and making positive life choices.

“Your decisions today shape your future,” Sanders told students. “Stay focused, surround yourself with the right people, and always remember your goals.”

The P.R.O.M. Promise—Please Return On Monday—is a signature initiative created by JSU’s Metro Jackson Community Prevention Coalition (MJCPC) designed to guide students in making informed, responsible decisions during prom season and beyond. The program addresses critical topics such as personal safety, peer pressure, mental and physical health, and post-secondary planning.

According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), distracted driving, especially texting or using social media while driving, is common among younger drivers. Statistics gathered by NHTSA documented that 3,275 people were killed in distraction-related crashes in 2023; 241 were teens, 15 to 19 years old.

“We started this initiative about 18 years ago. It started with small groups and has grown to this big event,” said Henry Thompson, director and principal investigator of MJCPC. “We’re trying to make sure these students return home safely without drinking and driving.”

Held on JSU’s campus, the event featured a rollover crash demonstration by the Mississippi Department of Transportation, a Q&A session with Sanders and a motivational speech from speaker Dwight Owens.

The high school students were also surprised by a live performance from Baton Rouge, Louisiana-based rapper H3adband. He performed his viral TikTok hit, “Boo,” which is currently on the Billboard Hot 100.

MJCPC emphasized that P.R.O.M. Promise is about preparing students for prom night and equipping them with tools for lifelong success. The program continues to grow each year, reinforcing JSU’s leadership in outreach and mentorship.

item.title: Rankin County Animal Shelter launches half-off adoption event as kennels fill up - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY – The Rankin County Animal Shelter is asking the public to adopt as it faces overcrowding and runs out of available kennel space.

Shelter officials said the facility is over capacity again and currently has no free kennels.

To help more pets find homes, the shelter is holding a half-off adoption event Friday and Saturday, March 27 and 28.

During the event, dog adoption fees will be reduced to $65. The fee includes spay or neuter services, a rabies vaccine, core vaccinations and a microchip, according to the shelter. Adopters also will receive a free collar and leash.

Shelter officials said the first eight adopters who take part in the special will also receive a gift card from The Cleaners by Pizza Shack.

The shelter is located at 710 Marquette Road in Brandon.

Officials encouraged people who cannot adopt to share the shelter’s message to help more animals find homes.

item.title: Mississippi wildlife officials conduct annual deer herd health evaluations across state - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Wildlife biologists in Mississippi have spent the past several weeks conducting annual deer herd health evaluations across the state to monitor reproduction, body condition and disease prevalence in mature female deer.

The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries and Parks said the evaluations are being carried out in partnership with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and Mississippi State University.

Officials said the surveys focus on female deer ages 2.5 years and older and are conducted each year on wildlife management areas, state parks, U.S. military lands and other public and private properties.

According to the department, the evaluations are especially important in areas where updated breeding data is needed, hunting pressure is limited, or herd changes are being monitored.

During the evaluations, biologists collect breeding data to determine peak rut timing, disease data including parasite loads and testing for epizootic hemorrhagic disease and chronic wasting disease, and body condition data such as weight and Kidney Fat Index.

Officials said the information helps track deer herd health over time and identify potential concerns, including low body weights or high parasite loads.

The department said all deer harvested during the evaluations are donated to charitable organizations, including Hunters for the Hungry and local food banks.

item.title: Mayor John Horhn Expresses Appreciation to Sheriff Tyree Jones - Darkhorse Press

item.description:
Statement from Mayor John Horhn on the service of Sheriff Tyree Jones as Jackson Police Chief:

I want to extend my thanks to Sheriff Tyree Jones for stepping up to lead the Jackson Police Department during an important time for our city. His leadership and understanding of both community needs and law enforcement helped ensure a smooth transition while we worked to identify our next chief.

I’m grateful for his willingness to take on this added responsibility in service to the people of Jackson. I look forward to our continued collaboration as we move forward working together.

We now welcome Dr. RaShall Brackney as our new Chief of Police. Her experience and strong record of leadership will bring valuable perspective to the department and further the city’s goals of safety, accountability, and community trust.

Thank you.

item.title: Madison County deputies seek public’s help in locating armed suspect - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MADISON COUNTY — The Madison County Sheriff’s Office is asking for the public’s help in locating a man wanted in connection with an aggravated assault involving a shooting, authorities said.

Antonio Harris, 31, is wanted after allegedly shooting a victim with a handgun, according to investigators. Deputies described Harris as a Black male, approximately 6 feet 2 inches tall and weighing about 200 pounds. He should be considered armed and dangerous.

Officials urged residents not to approach Harris and to contact law enforcement immediately with any information about his whereabouts.

Authorities said a reward of up to $2,500 may be available for information leading to Harris’ arrest. Tips can be submitted by calling Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS (8477) or online through its tip submission service.

No additional details about the shooting or the victim were immediately released. The investigation remains ongoing.

item.title: Dangerous gas leak forces closure of Bristol Crossing in Flowood - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
FLOWOOD – Bristol Crossing in Flowood has been completely shut down because of a gas leak, according to the Flowood Police Department.

Police said the combustion level in the area is dangerously high, and no vehicle or foot traffic is being allowed through the area.

Authorities said the school district has been notified so buses can use alternate routes for after-school drop-offs nearby.

Police said the estimated time for the road to reopen is 7 p.m.
